sources.title: Reading a visual language
sources.summary: Use a real catalog of portable preskins to learn families, contrast, mood and integrity-backed variation.
sources.boundary: A catalog proves what is declared and integrity-addressed; it does not prove that every skin suits every person or surface.

sources.title: From semantic mold to reusable organ
sources.summary: Study reusable molds, bounded moods and performance profiles from the generated mold-kit catalog.
sources.boundary: A generated mold is a reusable presentation structure, not proof of gameplay quality or universal compatibility.

sources.title: Build an Academy that can explain itself
sources.summary: Read the Learning Lab's own module contract to learn how teaching capabilities, handoffs, extension seams and explicit refusals remain inspectable.
sources.boundary: A module contract records declared interfaces and refusals; it does not prove runtime behavior, teaching quality, learner understanding or institutional authority.

sources.title: Atmosphere without hidden authority
sources.summary: Read the engine manifest as a lesson in visual power, reversible ownership and explicit guardrails.
sources.boundary: A manifest is a declared contract. Runtime behavior still needs tests and live visual evidence.

sources.title: Model a living world honestly
sources.summary: Use a living-world truth map to study conservation claims, explicit non-claims and the difference between a model and nature.
sources.boundary: Foundation Planet is a procedural exploration model, not a scientific Earth model, forecast or replacement for measured data.

sources.title: Preserve what an experiment taught
sources.summary: Learn how compact observations, rejected variants and contradictions can become reviewable design lessons.
sources.boundary: Repeated observations are not automatically taste, truth, vocabulary or canon; review remains explicit.
